name: Namatanai
reason: Rule 1/3: second town of New Ireland and Boluminski Highway terminus; Wikivoyage has an outline page with empty See/Do
objection: Case for: the highway end point and base for Tabar/Tigak trips, a regional hub. Case against: one source with no listed sight, only services.

name: Boluminski Highway
reason: Rule 1: PNG tourism board and Wikivoyage New Ireland both name the coast road (cycling the length, coral-surfaced, Fissoa waterholes) as the province's signature journey
objection: Strongest objection: a road is a journey not a place and the sights along it are separate; but both sources treat it as a Do, and it is a pin-able route at its midpoint.

name: Tabar Group
reason: Rule 1/2: PNG tourism lists the Tabar islands under remote escapes; single source, boat or flight access
objection: Case for: a named island group, Karanas itinerary. Against: one source, 'minimal tourist traffic', no stated thing to see.

name: Tatau Island
reason: Rule 1: Wikipedia only, no visitor source
objection: A part of the Tabar group, so even if wanted it would be folded into Tabar.

name: Lihir Group
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage New Ireland lists Lihir Island as an Other destination (gold-mine island, Air Niugini daily flights) and PNG tourism names it
objection: Against: mine island, little visitor infrastructure and the mine site is closed to the public; but two counted sources send visitors there and there is a scheduled flight.

name: Tanga Islands
reason: Rule 1: one counted source, in a list of remote island escapes
objection: Against: no described attraction; for: named by the tourism board.

name: Feni Islands
reason: Rule 1: PNG tourism page only mentions Feni in a geography sentence, not as somewhere to go
objection: For: a real island group with a boat route from Kavieng; against: no visitor source recommends it.

name: Tsoi Islands
reason: Rule 1: PNG tourism names the Tsoi islands in its remote escapes list and a photo caption
objection: Against: no attraction described and no Wikipedia article; for: tourism board lists it and a guesthouse operates.

name: Djaul Island
reason: Rule 1: no counted source
objection: Real island but nothing recommends visiting.

name: Nusa Island
reason: Rule 2: a resort island; the named draw is the Nusa Island Retreat seafood buffet and accommodation, a resort is never a spot
objection: For: two counted sources name it; against: they name the resort, not the island as a place to go.

name: Lissenung Island
reason: Rule 2: resort island; the sources point to Lissenung Island Resort (diving, crab platter)
objection: For: two sources, 20 minutes by boat; against: the resort is the whole draw.

name: Laraibina Eel Sanctuary
reason: Rule 1/2: PNG tourism eco-tour stop where visitors meet the revered eels; single source
objection: For: distinctive wildlife and culture stop. Against: one source, short visit, guided only, no location details.

name: Fissoa
reason: Rule 1/3: PNG tourism says explore Fissoa and other inland waterholes along the highway
objection: Against: one source and sits along the Boluminski Highway spot; for: named individually as a place to swim.

name: Deep Pete Wreck
reason: Rule 1: PNG tourism names the Mitsubishi F1M wreck dive off Kavieng, single source
objection: For: a named WWII wreck dive site, Kavieng's main draw is diving. Against: one source, accessible only to divers, appears only as a photo caption.

name: Borpop Airfield
reason: Rule 2: little is left visible; ten-minute look at best
objection: For: WWII site named by PNG tourism; against: one source and nothing to see.

name: Kavieng Rights Surf Break
reason: Rule 1: surf-forecast page only, no visitor guide
objection: Kavieng surfing is a Wikivoyage Do but this specific break is not named.

name: Libba Village
reason: Rule 1/2: no visitor source describes visiting
objection: Malagan carving is a draw, but the village is not named as a stop.

name: Lelet Plateau
reason: Rule 1: no visitor source
objection: Cultural area but nothing a visitor can do is documented.

name: Lombrum Naval Base
reason: Rule 2: active PNG Defence Force base, not open to visitors, and no visitor source
objection: For: WWII relics. Against: restricted military site (also the former asylum detention centre).

name: Pak Island
reason: Rule 1: Wikipedia only
objection: No visitor source.

name: Rambutyo Island
reason: Rule 1: Wikipedia only
objection: No visitor source.

name: Wuvulu Island
reason: Rule 1: re-looked; no counted source found (web search gave only a hotel-aggregator listing and Wikipedia); not in Wikivoyage Manus or the PNG tourism Manus page
objection: Strongest case against reject: Wuvulu is a known diving island; it should be re-checked for an operator's or PNG Dive page, and could go to review if a source turns up.

name: Aua Island
reason: Rule 1: no counted source
objection: Part of the Western Islands with Wuvulu; same objection.

name: Tuluman Island
reason: Rule 1/2: PNG tourism lists it in Manus MUST SEE (island born from a 1950s eruption)
objection: For: the tourism board's own headline for Manus. Against: single source, boat-only, access unclear.

name: Koruniat Island
reason: Rule 1: named only in a hotel's blurb about nearby attractions
objection: For: tourism site page; against: it is an accommodation listing, not a recommendation.

name: Loniu Passage
reason: Rule 1/3: hotel-listing mention only; a channel, not a thing to do
objection: Same objection as Koruniat.

name: Lou Island
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Manus lists it under Other destinations (traditional obsidian mining)
objection: Against: mining largely died out, one source, remote; for: it is the only named destination on the province page.

name: Buka Island
reason: Rule 1/2: Wikivoyage Bougainville/Buka name it the main arrival island with the market, waterfront and boat access to the Passage; gateway at low rank
objection: Against: Wikivoyage lists services, not sights; it is mainly a hub.

name: Buka Passage
reason: Rule 1/3: Wikivoyage See and do heading: boat trips through the channel for K2
objection: Against: a boat ride (vehicle), and Sohano is the place at the end; for: the main listed activity.

name: Sohano Island
reason: Rule 1/2: Wikivoyage names it the most visited island in the Passage: stroll, Japanese war memorial and plane wreck, eateries, K2 boat from Buka
objection: Against: one source and a half-hour stop; for: it is the described destination of the Passage trip.

name: Tchibo Rock
reason: Rule 3: a small feature on Sohano, part of the larger spot
objection: Strongest objection: Wikivoyage names it, but it is a minor legend rock.

name: Buka Market
reason: Rule 1/4: Wikivoyage Buy/Eat names a daily market with handicrafts and fish-on-a-stick; daily, so it passes rule 4
objection: Against: one source, short visit; for: daily market and the main thing to do in Buka town.

name: Kieta
reason: Rule 2: Wikivoyage mentions Kieta only as a port with transport links; nothing to see or do
objection: Port gateway; against reject: it is the ferry/airport town for Arawa.

name: Kokopau
reason: Rule 2/3: a landing village and start of the road
objection: Not named for anything to do.

name: Tinputz
reason: Rule 2: coastal village on the road, no listed draw
objection: Scenic road, but the village itself is not a described stop.

name: Panguna Mine
reason: Rule 2: no-go zone, reached only with a well-connected local per Wikivoyage; not open to the public
objection: One of the world's largest man-made holes and 17k views; but access is restricted.

name: Morgan Junction
reason: Rule 2: Wikivoyage lists it as a barricade to respect
objection: Not a stop.

name: Wakunai
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage names it as the base for the Mount Balbi trek and for buying basket-ware
objection: For: two Wikivoyage mentions. Against: a village of services.

name: Mount Balbi
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage calls the three-day Balbi trek the most popular serious trek; active volcano
objection: Against: single source, multi-day guided trek, remote; for: the region's headline outdoor draw.

name: Emperor Range
reason: Rule 3: the range is the trekking area and holds Balbi, a near-duplicate of the Balbi spot
objection: Against: the week-long crossing is described separately.

name: Mount Bagana
reason: Rule 3: Wikivoyage says it is visible from Balbi; not a visit target
objection: Very active volcano, but not offered as a stop.

name: Mount Billy Mitchell
reason: Rule 1/3: caldera lake reached on a trek extension
objection: For: Wikivoyage calls the lake beautiful. Against: a week-long extension, one source.

name: Yamamoto Bomber Wreck
reason: Rule 1/2: Wikivoyage: 'none more famous', signposted 3 km off the east coast road
objection: Against: one source and a short stop; for: a famous, signposted WWII site.

name: Nissan Island
reason: Rule 1: two Wikivoyage pages (Bougainville, Buka) call it the best-known outer island with an American WWII airstrip, relics and guesthouses
objection: Against: very remote, no booking lines; for: it has accommodation and a named draw.

name: Carteret Islands
reason: Rule 1/2: Wikivoyage names the Tulun Islands as an outer-island option
objection: Against: no facilities; sea-level-rise story but little to do; one source.

name: Cape Torokina
reason: Rule 1: re-looked; searches return only Wikipedia and Pacific Wrecks, no visitor source
objection: For: the 1943 landing site. Against: no counted source.

name: Buin
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Buka lists it as the southern town with Japanese base relics and the Yamamoto wreck
objection: Against: it is reached by a gravel track, one source, and the wreck is already its own spot.

name: Arawa
reason: Rule 1/2: Wikivoyage lists it as the former capital, largely derelict; base for Bougainville Experience Tours, with the Yamamoto wreck nearby; the town itself has no named sight (full-path: judged fresh after the audit disagreed with the script)

name: Kavieng
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage and PNG tourism both name it the gateway to New Ireland, with WWII relics, diving, surfing and fishing (full-path: judged fresh after the audit disagreed with the script)

name: Los Negros Island
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Manus only mentions its airport and causeway, PNG tourism only a nearby memorial park; no named thing to do (full-path: judged fresh after the audit disagreed with the script)

name: Manus Island
reason: Rule 1: PNG tourism and Wikivoyage name the island as the province's main place (Lorengau market, WWII relics, Garamut dance) (full-path: judged fresh after the audit disagreed with the script)

name: New Hanover Island
reason: Rule 1: sources mention the Three Island Harbour eco-lodge but give no sight; boat trip of a few hours from Kavieng (full-path: judged fresh after the audit disagreed with the script)

name: Buka
reason: Wikivoyage Bougainville names Buka as the hub town with market, tourist office and the Buka Passage boat trips, which it calls a key visitor attraction; a harbour town a guide recommends as a stop. (full-path: judged fresh after the audit disagreed with the script)

name: Lorengau
reason: Wikivoyage has its own Lorengau page and papuanewguinea.travel covers it as Manus Province's capital and gateway; a regional hub town earns a low-rank spot, though its sights are thin (market, WWII relics around the harbour). (full-path: judged fresh after the audit disagreed with the script)

name: Malagan Carvings
reason: A cultural tradition and ceremonies, not a place a visitor can walk up to at any time; ceremonies are events and there is no fixed venue. Any real venue (carving village, workshop) should be judged on its own. (full-path: judged fresh after the audit disagreed with the script)

name: Momote Memorial Park
reason: Single source is a hotel listing on the tourism page; a minor WWII memorial with no guide naming it as a stop and no half-hour activity. (full-path: judged fresh after the audit disagreed with the script)

name: Seeadler Harbour
reason: For: Wikivoyage Lorengau and papuanewguinea.travel both name it, and WWII relics can still be seen around it. Against: it is a water body with no defined visitor spot or activity, largely the setting of Lorengau; keep only if the owner wants it as a relics or boat-trip stop, otherwise fold into Lorengau.
